heading.en: When the government fixes the price

title.en: Explain price ceiling and its consequences
Explain price floor and its consequences

say.en: Ration shops sell rice below the market price; the government buys wheat from farmers at a minimum support price. What happens to demand and supply then? In this lesson: Explain price ceiling and its consequences.
Explain price floor and its consequences.

body.en: A price ceiling is a maximum price fixed by the government, below the equilibrium price, to make essential goods (food grains, kerosene, cooking gas) affordable. At the ceiling, quantity demanded exceeds quantity supplied: a shortage (excess demand). The government then uses rationing (ration cards, fair price shops) to share the limited supply. Problems: long queues, poorer quality, and black markets where the good is sold illegally at higher prices.

points.en: Risks: queues, black market, lower quality

narration.en: A price ceiling is a maximum price below equilibrium. It creates a shortage, which leads to rationing and often a black market.
narration.kn: ಗರಿಷ್ಠ ಬೆಲೆ ಮಿತಿ ಸಮತೋಲನ ಬೆಲೆಗಿಂತ ಕಡಿಮೆ ನಿಗದಿಪಡಿಸಿದ ಗರಿಷ್ಠ ಬೆಲೆ. ಇದು ಕೊರತೆ ಉಂಟುಮಾಡುತ್ತದೆ; ಪಡಿತರ ವ್ಯವಸ್ಥೆ ಮತ್ತು ಕಾಳಸಂತೆಗೆ ಕಾರಣವಾಗುತ್ತದೆ.

say.en: Equilibrium is at price 10 and quantity 200. Now the government sets a ceiling at 6, below equilibrium.
At 6, buyers want 240 but sellers offer only 140. The gap of 100 is the shortage.
Now a floor at 14, above equilibrium. Sellers offer 260 but buyers want only 160: a surplus of 100.

body.en: A price floor is a minimum price fixed above the equilibrium price, to protect producers or workers. Examples: the Minimum Support Price (MSP) for crops and minimum wages. At the floor, quantity supplied exceeds quantity demanded: a surplus (excess supply). The government usually buys the surplus to build buffer stocks, which costs money and needs storage; with minimum wages, the surplus of labour means unemployment.

narration.en: A price floor is a minimum price above equilibrium. It creates a surplus, which the government often buys up, as with MSP for wheat.
